evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The `manager_restarted` condition verifies only nonempty, differing manager PIDs and invocation IDs. It never requires the before/after manager snapshots to share a boot ID, so a guest reboot occurring between the restart command and the second inspect can change both PID and invocation ID and satisfy the check even though the restart was not isolated. The separate `boot_id_changed` check covers the planned reboot snapshots, not this manager snapshot pair. Requiring nonempty equal boot IDs in `manager.before` and `manager.after` while retaining the PID and invocation checks is the smallest correctness fix.
